title: Regular Expression Matching
statement:
Implement a tiny regular-expression matcher. You are given a text `s` and a pattern `p`. The pattern supports two special characters:

- `.` matches **any single** character.
- `*` matches **zero or more** copies of the character immediately before it. That preceding character is either a lowercase letter or `.` (so `.*` matches any string, including the empty one).

The match must cover the **entire** text `s`, not just a part of it. Print `true` if the whole of `s` matches `p`, otherwise `false`.

It is guaranteed that `*` never appears as the first character of `p` and never directly follows another `*`.

**Follow-up:** a 2026 Zoho online assessment reportedly used `+` (one or more of the preceding character) together with `*` instead of the `.`/`*` pair. After solving this version, think about how you would adapt your transition for `+`.
input_format:
The first line contains the text `s`.
The second line contains the pattern `p`.
output_format: Print `true` if `p` matches the entire string `s`, otherwise print `false`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
p consists of lowercase English letters, `.` and `*`; every `*` follows a letter or `.`

examples.explanation: `z*` takes the first three `z`. Then `.` matches the final `y`, and `y*` matches zero characters. Everything is consumed, so the answer is true.
`c` matches `c`. `.*` must stop before a `b`, which can only be at index 2. `b` matches it and `b*` matches nothing, but the final `d` is left unmatched. No other split works, so the answer is false.
`.*` can match any string, including the single character `k`.

hints: Try a recursive definition on the first characters of `s` and `p`. The tricky case is when the next pattern character is `*`: you can either skip the `x*` pair entirely or consume one matching character of `s` and stay on the same pair.
Plain recursion repeats the same (position in s, position in p) subproblems exponentially often on patterns like `a*a*a*b`. Memoize it, or build a table `dp[i][j]` = does `s[:i]` match `p[:j]`.

Initialise `dp[0][j]` for patterns that can match the empty string (`a*b*`). For `p[j-1] == '*'`: `dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-2]` (zero copies) or, if `p[j-2]` matches `s[i-1]`, `dp[i-1][j]`. Only the previous row is needed.
brute:
import sys, re

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
s, p = data[0], data[1]
print('true' if re.fullmatch(p, s) else 'false')
